# Getting started

## Prerequisites

:::{.rmdnote}
**Minimum system requirements:**

-   Windows 10, macOS 11 Big Sur, or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS;
-   20 GB of storage space, plus additional storage for model outputs;
-   128 GB RAM to run the model over the full area (less for sub-areas);
-   High-speed internet connection.
:::

The following section provides details on installing prerequisite software for running LandWeb.

### Docker

:::{.rmdwarning}
Due to idiosyncratic difficulties of installing multiple pieces of software and ensuring the correct versions are used throughout, we provide prebuilt [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) images, which better provides a consistent and reproducible software environment for running the model.

Thus, using these images are preferred over 'bare-metal' installation.

**If you prefer to not use Docker, skip this subsection.**
:::

Install Docker for your system following <https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/>.

The image runs LandWeb in Rstudio Server.
It holds R at the version in `renv.lock` (R 4.6.1), the project's R packages, TeX Live and Quarto for the reports, and the LandWeb code with its submodules.
It holds no data and no credentials.
GitHub Actions builds it from the `rocker/geospatial` image (`.github/workflows/docker-image.yaml`) and publishes it to the GitHub Container Registry.

Pull the image:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/predictiveecology/landweb:latest
```

`latest` is the newest build of the `main` branch, or the newest release.
Each release also has its own tag (*e.g.*, `3.0.0`), and each monthly rebuild of `main` a dated one (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

Launch a container from the image, with your `inputs/` and `outputs/` directories mounted from the host (adjust the two paths, `PASSWORD`, `memory`, and `cpus` as needed):

```bash
INPUTS_HOST=/path/to/LandWeb/inputs
OUTPUTS_HOST=/path/to/LandWeb/outputs
PROJ_CONTAINER=/home/rstudio/GitHub/LandWeb

docker run -d -it \
  -e USERID=$(id -u) \
  -e GROUPID=$(id -g) \
  -e PASSWORD='<mySecretPassword>' \
  -e GITHUB_PAT=$(grep GITHUB_PAT ~/.Renviron | cut -d '=' -f 2) \
  --memory=128g \
  --cpus=32 \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8787 \
  --mount type=bind,source=$INPUTS_HOST,target=$PROJ_CONTAINER/inputs \
  --mount type=bind,source=$OUTPUTS_HOST,target=$PROJ_CONTAINER/outputs \
  --name landweb01 \
  ghcr.io/predictiveecology/landweb:latest
```

- `USERID` and `GROUPID` make the container's `rstudio` user your own user, so the files written to the mounted directories belong to you.
- `GITHUB_PAT` is needed only to install further packages from GitHub inside the container.

Once the container is running, open your web browser and go to `localhost:8080`.
Log in to the Rstudio session as user `rstudio` with the password you set above.
If the container runs on a remote machine, forward the port first:

```bash
ssh <host> -L8080:localhost:8080
```

A pipeline run inside the container downloads data as the LandWeb service account, so it needs the key file described in [Data requirements].

Once finished, stop and remove the container:

```bash
docker stop landweb01
docker rm landweb01
```

`docker/LandWeb-standalone_README.md` describes the image in more detail, including how to build it yourself.

### Bare metal installation

#### Development tools

##### Windows

1. `Rtools` provides the necessary compilers etc. to build and install R packages from source on Windows. It will be installed alongside R following the instructions in the section below.

2. Download and install a proper text editor, *e.g.* `Notepad++` (<https://notepad-plus-plus.org/downloads/>).

```shell
winget install Notepad++.Notepad++
```

##### macOS

###### Xcode command line tools

To build software, you will need the Xcode command line tools[^xcode], which include various compilers and `git` version control software.

[^xcode]: <https://developer.apple.com/downloads/>

```zsh
xcode-select --install
```

###### `homebrew` package manager

Next, install `homebrew` which provides a package manager for macOS.
This will facilitate software updates and will handle various package dependency issues automatically.

```zsh
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

##### Ubuntu Linux

Install the build tools, and TeX Live for the PDF reports and manual:

```bash
sudo apt-get update

sudo apt-get -y install \
    biber \
    build-essential \
    ccache \
    cmake \
    curl \
    git \
    make \
    pandoc \
    qpdf \
    texinfo texlive-base texlive-bibtex-extra \
    texlive-fonts-extra texlive-latex-extra texlive-xetex \
    unzip \
    wget \
    xauth \
    xfonts-base \
    xvfb
```

The system libraries that LandWeb's R packages need are installed once R and the code are in place (see [System libraries for R packages on Ubuntu](#sysreqs)).

#### Geospatial libraries

In order to work with geospatial data, recent versions of `GDAL`, `PROJ`, and `GEOS` geospatial libraries need to be available on your system.

##### Windows

No additional should be needed, as recent versions of R geospatial packages include pre-bundled versions of `GDAL`, `PROJ`, and `GEOS`.

##### macOS

Use `homebrew` to install the required geospatial software libraries:

```zsh
brew install pkg-config
brew install gdal
brew install ghostscript
# brew install geos
# brew install proj
brew install imagemagick
brew install udunits
```

##### Ubuntu Linux

Install the geospatial libraries from Ubuntu's own package repositories, as the project's continuous integration and Docker image do.
Ubuntu 24.04 and later ship versions recent enough for LandWeb, so no extra repository is needed.

```bash
sudo apt-get -y install \
    gdal-bin \
    libgdal-dev \
    libgeos-dev \
    libproj-dev \
    libsqlite3-dev \
    libudunits2-dev \
    pkg-config
```

:::{.rmdcaution}
Do not add the `ubuntugis` PPA.
It installs a newer GDAL than Ubuntu's own, and the prebuilt Linux R packages from Posit Package Manager, which are built against Ubuntu's GDAL, then fail to load (*e.g.*, "`libgdal.so.34`: cannot open shared object file").
:::

#### R and Rstudio

1. Download and install R version 4.6.1, using `rig` (<https://github.com/r-lib/rig>), which simplifies management of multiple R installations, and allows easy switching among them.


:::{.rmdimportant}
**Windows**

1. Install `rig`:

```shell
winget install posit.rig
```

2. Install R:

```shell
rig add 4.6.1
rig system make-links
rig system rtools install 45
```

**macOS**

1. Install `rig`:

```zsh
brew tap r-lib/rig
brew install --cask rig
```

2. Install R:

```zsh
rig add 4.6.1

rig system fix-permissions
rig system make-links
rig system make-orthogonal
rig system setup-user-lib
```

**Ubuntu Linux**

1. Install `rig`:

```bash
## add apt repository
sudo curl -L https://rig.r-pkg.org/deb/rig.gpg -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/rig.gpg
sudo sh -c "echo 'deb [arch=amd64] http://rig.r-pkg.org/deb rig main' > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/rig.list"

## install (NB: rig is different package; use r-rig!)
sudo apt update
sudo apt install r-rig
```

2. Install R:

```bash
rig add 4.6.1

rig system make-links

sudo ln -s /opt/R/4.6.1/bin/Rscript /usr/local/bin/Rscript-4.6.1

rig list
```
:::

2. Download and install the latest version of Rstudio from <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>.

:::{.rmdimportant}
Windows users should install Rstudio *as administrator*.
:::

3. (optional) On Linux, configure `ccache` to speed up R package re-installation and updates[^ccache].

    ```bash
    ## configure ccache for R package installation
    mkdir -p ~/.ccache
    mkdir -p ~/.R
    { echo 'VER='; \
      echo 'CCACHE=ccache'; \
      echo 'CC=$(CCACHE) gcc$(VER)'; \
      echo 'CXX=$(CCACHE) g++$(VER)'; \
      echo 'CXX11=$(CCACHE) g++$(VER)'; \
      echo 'CXX14=$(CCACHE) g++$(VER)'; \
      echo 'FC=$(CCACHE) gfortran$(VER)'; \
      echo 'F77=$(CCACHE) gfortran$(VER)'; } >> ~/.R/Makevars
    { echo 'max_size = 5.0G'; \
      echo 'sloppiness = include_file_ctime'; \
      echo 'hash_dir = false'; } >> ~/.ccache/ccache.conf
    ```

[^ccache]: <http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2017/11/27/#011_faster_package_installation_one>

#### Quarto

The LandWeb reports (`reports/*.qmd`) are rendered with Quarto (<https://quarto.org>), including the study area report that each run builds.
Install Quarto 1.9.38, the version the project's tests use (`.github/workflows/tests.yaml`); another version can lay out page breaks in the PDF reports differently.

:::{.rmdimportant}
**Windows**

```shell
winget install --id Posit.Quarto --version 1.9.38
```

**macOS**

```zsh
curl -LO https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.9.38/quarto-1.9.38-macos.pkg
sudo installer -pkg quarto-1.9.38-macos.pkg -target /
```

**Ubuntu Linux**

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/releases/download/v1.9.38/quarto-1.9.38-linux-amd64.deb
sudo apt-get install ./quarto-1.9.38-linux-amd64.deb
```
:::

The reports are PDFs, so Quarto also needs LaTeX.
On Ubuntu, the TeX Live packages installed above provide it.
On Windows and macOS, install TinyTeX with Quarto:

```bash
quarto install tinytex
```

Check the installation with `quarto check`.

#### Version control

`git` is the version control software used throughout this project, and is required to 'checkout' specific versions of the code as well as to make changes and 'push' these changes to the model code repository.

1. Install the latest version of `git` from <https://git-scm.com/downloads> or via your package manager.
    
:::{.rmdimportant}
Windows users should install *as administrator*.
Use `nano` (instead of `vi`/`vim`) as the default text editor.
For all other choices, use the recommended settings.

For macOS users, `git` is included with the Xcode command line tools.
:::

2. Create a GitHub (<https://github.com>) account if you don't already have one, and configure a Personal Access Token (PAT).

:::{.rmdwarning}
A GitHub (<https://github.com>) account is required to assist with package installation and accessing model code.
:::

Several packages used by LandWeb are only available on GitHub.
Because we will be installing several of these, we want to ensure we can do so without GitHub rate-limiting our requests.
Without a PAT, some packages may *temporarily* fail to install, but can be retried a little later (usually 1 hour).

a.  Create a GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT):

    i. either 'manually' following the instructions[^GH_PAT], making sure to check the `repo`, `workflow`, and `user:email` scopes;

    ii. or directly from an R session:

        ```r
        # install.packages("usethis")
        usethis::create_github_token()
        ```

b.  Securely store this token using the credential store, from an R session:

    ```r
    > gitcreds::gitcreds_set()
    
    ? Enter password or token: ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
    -> Adding new credentials...
    -> Removing credentials from cache...
    -> Done.
    ```
    
:::{.rmdwarning}
**Storing GitHub credentials in `.Renviron` is no longer recommended for Windows / macOS.**

See <https://usethis.r-lib.org/articles/git-credentials.html>.
:::

3.  *Optional.* Install the latest version of `GitKraken` from <https://www.gitkraken.com/download/>.

:::{.rmdimportant}
The free version is sufficient to access the public repositories used in this project.
However, the paid pro version is required to access private repositories.
:::
    
[^GH_PAT]: <https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/creating-a-personal-access-token>

## Getting the code

All modules are written in R and all model code was developed collaboratively using GitHub (<https://github.com>), with each module contained in its own repository.
Code that is shared among modules was bundled into R packages, and hosted in on GitHub repositories.
All package code is automatically and regularly tested using cross-platform continuous integration frameworks to ensure the code is reliable and free of errors.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/GitHub
cd ~/GitHub

## get the development branch, with its submodules
git clone -b development --recurse-submodules \
  -j8  https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/LandWeb
```

### Home directories on Windows {#windows-home}

The paths used to set up LandWeb on Windows assume the usual Windows home directories:

- R's home directory (`~` in R and Rstudio) is `C:/Users/<name>/Documents`;
- the home directory of Git Bash and other terminals is `C:/Users/<name>`.

`~/GitHub` therefore names a different directory in R than in a terminal.
Make the clone reachable from both by creating a directory junction, in a Command Prompt window:

```shell
mklink /J C:\Users\<name>\Documents\GitHub C:\Users\<name>\GitHub
```

Paths that R reads, such as the Google service account key in [Data requirements], start from R's home directory.

:::{.rmdimportant}
**Corporate machines with OneDrive**

Some corporate Windows machines move the Documents folder to OneDrive (*e.g.*, `C:/Users/<name>/OneDrive - <Company>/Documents`), and R's home directory moves with it.
Check where yours is, from R:

```r
normalizePath("~")
```

If it is not `C:\Users\<name>\Documents`, set the environment variable `R_USER` to that folder.
R uses `R_USER` as its home directory whenever it is set, ahead of the Documents folder, so this restores the usual setup.
Set it as a Windows user environment variable, either in a Command Prompt or PowerShell window:

```shell
setx R_USER "C:\Users\<name>\Documents"
```

or from the Start menu, under *Edit environment variables for your account*.
Do not set it in an `.Renviron` file: R finds `.Renviron` in its home directory, so by the time the file is read the home directory is already set.
Create the folder if it does not exist, then restart Rstudio and any open terminals so that they pick up the new value.
:::

### System libraries for R packages on Ubuntu {#sysreqs}

The R packages LandWeb uses need further system libraries.
Derive the list from the project's lockfile (`renv.lock`) and install it, as the project's continuous integration and Docker image do (`.github/scripts/sysreqs.R`).
The script needs the `renv` package, which is installed here into a temporary library:

```bash
cd ~/GitHub/LandWeb
mkdir -p /tmp/sysreqs-lib
Rscript-4.6.1 --vanilla -e 'install.packages("renv", lib = "/tmp/sysreqs-lib", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
R_LIBS=/tmp/sysreqs-lib Rscript-4.6.1 --vanilla .github/scripts/sysreqs.R renv.lock /tmp/sysreqs.txt

sudo apt-get update
xargs -a /tmp/sysreqs.txt sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends
```

## Project directory structure

Model code is organized by the following directories and summarized in the table below.

:::{.rmdtip}
It may be useful to store data in a different location, but to map this location back to the `inputs/` and/or `outputs/` directories using symbolic links.
See R's `?file.link` to set these up on your machine.
:::

```{r dir-structure-setup, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, results = 'hide'}
prjDir <- SpaDES.config::findProjectPath(from_wd = FALSE)

## create these directories if they don't exist (e.g., GHA)
file.path(prjDir, c("inputs", "outputs")) |>
  fs::dir_create()
```

```{r dir-structure, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE}
## NB: look descriptions up BY NAME rather than pairing a hardcoded vector against a live
## directory listing -- the latter broke the build whenever a top-level directory was added
## (v3 added `_targets/`, `reports/`, `logs/`, `citations/`, ... -> 19 dirs vs 12 descriptions,
## "arguments imply differing number of rows"). Unknown directories now degrade gracefully.
local({
  descriptions <- c(
    "R" = "R functions used by the pipeline and reports",
    "_targets" = "`targets` pipeline store (metadata + cached objects)",
    "citations" = "bibliographies and citation styles",
    "docker" = "Dockerfile and documentation",
    "docs" = "rendered manual",
    "inputs" = "all model data inputs stored here",
    "logs" = "run and worker logs",
    "manual" = "raw files for generating documentation manual",
    "modules" = "module code (git submodules)",
    "outputs" = "all per-run model outputs stored here",
    "outputs_v2" = "archived LandWeb v2 outputs (reference for v2-vs-v3 comparisons)",
    "packages" = "package code (git submodules)",
    "renv" = "project package management directory",
    "reports" = "automated Quarto reports",
    "scripts" = "standalone utility scripts",
    "tests" = "tests of the project's R functions and reports"
  )
  dirs <- fs::dir_ls(prjDir, recurse = 0, type = c("directory", "symlink")) |> fs::path_file()
  data.frame(
    directory = paste0(dirs, "/"),
    description = unname(ifelse(dirs %in% names(descriptions), descriptions[dirs], ""))
  )
}) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "LandWeb project directory structure", booktabs = TRUE) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "scale_down"))
```

## Updating the code

After having cloned the LandWeb code repository, users can keep up-to-date using their preferred graphical git tools (*e.g.*, GitKraken) or from the command line.

### Using GitKraken

```{r gitkraken-screen, eval = TRUE, echo = FALSE, fig.align = "center", fig.cap = "Screenshot showing showing code commits in Git Kraken. The submodules pane is highlighted on the bottom left.", fig.width = 6, out.width = "90%"}
knitr::include_graphics(Require::normPath(c("figures/gitkraken1.png")))
```

1.  Open the LandWeb repo, and after a few moments you will see the commit history update to reflect the latest changes on the server.

2.  'Pull' in the latest changes to this repo, noting that the status of the git submodules (left hand side) may change.

3.  If any submodules have changed status, for each one, right-click and select 'Update <module name>'.

### Using the command line

**WARNING:** experienced git users only!

```bash
git pull
git submodule update
```

## Data requirements

In order to access and use the proprietary data in LandWeb simulations, you will need to be granted access to the shared Google Drive directory.
During first-run of the model, all required data will be downloaded to the `inputs/` directory.

To request access, please contact Alex Chubaty ([achubaty\@for-cast.ca](mailto:achubaty@for-cast.ca){.email}).

Pipeline runs (`targets::tar_make()` and its workers) download as the LandWeb Google service account, not as you.
Its key file is never kept in the repository.
On every machine that runs the pipeline, store it as `~/.config/landweb/drive-sa.json`, readable only by you (`chmod 700 ~/.config/landweb` and `chmod 600` on the file).
Then create an untracked `LandWeb.Renviron` in the project root containing the single line `GOOGLEDRIVE_AUTH=~/.config/landweb/drive-sa.json`.
On Windows, `~` in this path is R's home directory (see [Home directories on Windows](#windows-home)).
At startup, `.Rprofile` ignores Google key paths set anywhere else (such as `~/.Renviron`), reads `LandWeb.Renviron`, and refuses a key that is not from the LandWeb Google Cloud project.
Interactive sessions use your own Google login.
